prompt:
## Output and source
Return one bare JSON object with exactly five keys: "name", "phone", "email", "company", "country". Every value is a string or JSON null. No other text, fences, or keys.

The user's message is a note containing one contact record. Read only its label/value lines. Recognize label variants, arbitrary line order, and colon, equals, or tab separators with optional whitespace. Do not extract values from surrounding notes or signatures, or infer fields from email domains or company suffixes.

## 1. Prepare and assign values
Trim each value and collapse whitespace runs to one space. Absent or blank values and whole-value placeholders (-, --, n/a, na, none, unknown, ?, null, TBD, any case) are missing. Missing fields are null except for the country fallback below.

A value containing @ is the email, regardless of label. A value is the phone if, after stripping a leading tel: and a trailing extension marked by ext., ext, x, #, or extension followed by digits, it contains at least seven digits and only digits, spaces and + - ( ) . /. Use name and company labels unless the name-line value ends with a legal suffix from the list below and the company-line value does not; in that case swap the two before normalizing either.

## 2. Resolve country and phone
Take country from the country line and convert it to uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Accept country names in English, Swedish or German, alpha-2 and alpha-3 codes, and aliases in any case: UK and Great Britain → GB; Holland → NL; USA and U.S.A. → US; Türkiye → TR; Czech Republic → CZ.

Strip tel: and the extension before formatting the phone. Check its prefix before stripping punctuation. Ignoring a leading opening parenthesis, a leading + or 00 means international. Convert a leading 00 to +, remove (0), and strip spaces, dashes, dots, slashes and parentheses. Keep the written calling code even if it differs from the country line. Only if the country is missing, fill it from an international phone's calling code when that code belongs to exactly one country. Shared codes, including +1 and +7, leave country null.

For a national phone, strip formatting punctuation and remove one leading trunk 0. Prepend + and the calling code of the normalized record country. If the country is missing, set the national phone to null. A non-null phone is E.164: +, calling code, national significant number, with no characters other than digits after +.

## 3. Normalize name, company and email
Name: For Last, First, split at the first comma and put First before Last. Drop leading Dr, Mr, Mrs, Ms, Mx, or Prof, optionally dotted and in any case. Uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space- or hyphen-separated part. Keep Unicode letters and diacritics; never transliterate.

Company: Remove a trailing legal suffix and its optional preceding comma. Match case-insensitively against AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda. Trim, then uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space-separated word.

Email: Remove a mailto: prefix and surrounding angle brackets, then lowercase the entire address.

Emit the five-key JSON object. The country fallback is the only exception to the rule against filling missing values.
